title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 48 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. It immediately follows the computation on p.427, where the equation ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 in the profinite group Π̂_{0,3} forced ν=±1.

Grothendieck now moves to a linear model: an affine group scheme G over a ring A, for example SL(2)_Z or GL(2)_Z, with a section ρ.

- **The map.** He studies F_ρ: G→G, α ↦ αρ(α)^{-1} = [α,ρ]. Here ρ(α) means the inner action ραρ^{-1}, so F_ρ(α) = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1}. This is the commutator map, or 'Lang-type' map, attached to the inner automorphism int(ρ).
- **Fibres.** If T_ρ = Centr_G(ρ) = G^ρ is the centralizer subgroup scheme, then F_ρ(α') = F_ρ(α) iff α' is a section of αT_ρ. Indeed α'ρα'^{-1} = αρα^{-1} iff α^{-1}α' centralizes ρ.
- **Monomorphism.** Hence F_ρ induces a monomorphism of fppf sheaves G/T_ρ ↪ G, identifying the quotient with the orbit map α ↦ αρα^{-1} followed by right translation by ρ^{-1}.
- **Image problem.** The task is to characterize the image of this monomorphism.
- **First necessary condition.** Let δ: G→G_ab be the abelianization. In the cases of interest it is representable: trivial for SL2 (perfect as a group scheme), and G_m via det for GL2. A point ξ ∈ G(S), for an A-scheme S, can lie in the image only if δ(ξ)=1, since ξ is a commutator.
- **Second condition (next page).** ξρ must be locally conjugate to ρ. This is necessary and sufficient, and it leads to Steinberg's invariant quotient G→I_G (the adjoint quotient) for reductive G.

The purpose seems to be to build a group scheme or algebraic model in which equations like ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1, i.e. conditions on the 'lacets', can be analysed through conjugacy classes in a linear group.
errors: No real error. Minor points: the notation ρ(α) is ambiguous; it must mean int(ρ)(α)=ραρ^{-1}, and on the previous page ρ was an automorphism of Π̂_{0,3}, not a section. G/T_ρ must be taken as an fppf (or fpqc) sheaf quotient, and the monomorphism is a monomorphism of sheaves. On this page the condition is written Δ(ξ)=1, while the next page calls the map δ.
Representability of G_ab is asserted only for the examples, which is correct: SL2 has trivial abelianization as a group scheme even though the abstract group SL2(Z) has abelianization Z/12.

ideas.what: Commutator map α↦αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} with fibres equal to cosets of the centralizer, giving a monomorphism G/Z_G(ρ)↪G
ideas.modern_name: orbit map / conjugacy-class embedding; twisted (Lang-type) map for an inner automorphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (SGA3-type orbit arguments; Lang, Steinberg for twisted maps)
ideas.where_published: SGA3 (quotients, centralizers, orbit morphisms) in general form

ideas.what: Necessary condition for being a commutator: trivial image in the abelianization G_ab (trivial for SL2, det for GL2)
ideas.modern_name: abelianization / derived group of a group scheme

ideas.what: Using a linear group scheme (SL2_Z, GL2_Z) as a testing ground for the loop equation ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 from the Teichmüller-tower / GT context
ideas.modern_name: linear (SL2) representations of Π̂_{0,3} and of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type equations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Drinfeld, and later work on GT acting on SL2 / modular representations

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins constructing a group scheme to parametrize solutions of the loop equation inside SL2/GL2 over Z. Solutions ξ are to be described as commutators [α,ρ], characterized via local conjugacy and Steinberg's adjoint quotient. This suggests an 'algebraic-group model' of the équation des lacets over Spec Z that has not been developed as such.
missed.quote: 48. Construction d'un schéma en groupes ... dont il s'agit de caractériser l'image.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could connect GT-type equations to character varieties and adjoint quotients over Z (Steinberg map). This is a scheme-theoretic analogue of studying GT via SL2 representations, but the page itself is only the routine setup.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is standard: orbit maps, centralizers, and the abelianization obstruction. The only interest is contextual, namely the idea of modelling the loop equation in an algebraic group scheme over Z, which is only begun here.
transcription_corrections: Condition (4) is written Δ(ξ)=1 (capital), while the next page uses δ for the map G→G_ab.
'Sl(2)_Z' has a struck-out subscript before the Z.
